To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and IL-6 are important mediators of the senescence-associated inflammatory microenvironment and are responsible for the emergence and reinforcement of tumorigenic and stemness-related features in the MCF7 cell line.

IL6 and IL-IL8 are major mediators of the senescence/inflammation-induced EMT and stem cell features, and that these cytokines also play an important role in maintaining aggressive traits in a highly tumorigenetic breast cancer cell line.
IL6 and IL-IL8 induce a senescence/inflammation milieu in MCF-7 which reinforces tumorigenic traits and that the aggressive phenotype of MDA-MB231 is maintained by the same mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL-6 and -8 in the emergence of stem-like features in a less aggressive breast cancer model.

the role of senescence and the SASP on the acquisition of stemness and EMT-related features by MCF- 7 breast cancer cells, and with their role on the maintenance of the aggressive phenotype of the MDA-MB 231 cell line.

the role of IL-6 and 8 in senescence-associated inflammation, which is a major contributor to the acquisition of aggressive phenotypes, and may be a potential target to prevent tumorigenic progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
senescence, inflammation, EMT and stem cells are all intertwined, and the interplay among them is crucial to tumour development.

the acquisition of stem-like features by MCF-10A cells in the presence of IL-6 and/or IL-8 is associated with a more aggressive phenotype and that the aggressiveness of MDA-MB231 cells is also IL6/IL8-dependent, although these cells lack stem-like features.
the SASP and its mediators IL6 and IL-6, are key players in the acquisition of aggressive traits by breast cancer cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

senescence-associated cytokines are important to promote tumour aggressiveness, but not necessarily through the acquisition of stem-like features, and that IL6 and IL-6 are important to maintain tumour aggressiveness in both luminal and basal-like breast cancer cells.

senescence and senescence-associated inflammation are reinforcing mechanisms that favour the acquisition of E-M transition and stemness features at the population levels, thus increasing tumoral aggressiveness.
IL6 and IL-6 are important mediators of senescence and stemness-related phenotypes, but the relationship among senescence, inflammation, EMT and stem cell properties is not always straightforward.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inflammatory microenvironment is a key player in the acquisition of tumorigenic traits in breast cancer cells.
the SASP is an important contributor to the acquisition of EpiSC features, and that the inflammatory microenvironment is a major driving force in the progression towards malignancy.

the senescence-related SASP is a major player in the acquisition of aggressive phenotypic features, which is not only limited to senescent cells but is also extended to neighbouring cells, including cancer cells.
